title: Eastern Polynesian: The linguistic evidence revisited
notes: Re-examines the Marquesic and Tahitic subgroups (§4) and proposes a tree with no Proto-Marquesic or Proto-Tahitic: every Central Eastern Polynesian language directly under PCEP (Figure 2, p. 268). Its Table 1 (p. 261) is adapted from Marck (2000: 24-26).

author: Wilson, William H.
title: East Polynesian subgrouping and homeland implications within the Northern Outlier–East Polynesian hypothesis
notes: Places East Polynesian under Proto-Central Northern Outlier-East Polynesian and splits PEPN into Distal (Marquesan, and PFEPN: Mangarevan, Rapa Nui) and Proximal (Hawaiian; PEPNP(S) = Proto-Tahitic) dialects (Figures 1-2, p. 42; Table 1, p. 38). Assumes one phoneme inventory for PNPN, PCNO-EPN, PEPN and its descendants, with the regular reflexes of Marck (2000: 23-24, 74) (p. 44); the evidence is lexical and grammatical, with irregular changes in single words. Glottolog 5.4 follows this tree.
